overall_assessment:
No concrete severe server/runtime performance blocker was identified in the embedded candidate. PERF-R6-01 is resolved: the materialized parent page precedes operation hydration, and the supplied PostgreSQL plans show child lookups limited to returned drafts, including zero lookups beyond the last page. OPS-R6-02 also has substantive correction and executed browser evidence. One residual asynchronous UI state-write defect is reported below as nonblocking for this performance dispatch.

Performance: local lists execute one bounded hydration query plus a scoped count; detail hydration returns at most 11 operations and 10 receipts per operation; catalog hydration performs at most 50 indexed probes within one SQL statement. These database execution loops are bounded joins, not application request loops. Provider submission/preflight/recovery paths have explicit page, call, byte and timeout limits. Exact remote-ID reads use the individual endpoint. The approved filtered-name preflight/recovery exception remains bounded to two pages and fails inconclusively rather than walking the catalog. HTTP stays outside database transactions, credential metadata checks use the transaction connection, and submission quotas are durable. Deep OFFSET and exact counts retain cardinality-dependent parent work, but the evidence does not establish a severe risk warranting reopening the approved pagination contract. Catalog writes are bounded to 50 upserts; batching them would be optimization debt, not a blocker.

Concurrency and load evidence: the actual template FRC marker establishes 100 BFF requests, 99 lease-blocked 202 responses, one provider-list leader and one completed, nonempty 200 response. PostgreSQL tests exercise CAS, global name coordination, commit uncertainty, recovery and late ACK ordering. The five waves of 20 independent intents demonstrate concurrency across distinct resources; they do not independently prove 20 contenders on one resource. The five-tenant RLS stage supports bounded functional load behavior, without a latency, capacity or production claim. This review does not convert the pending TODO lane rows into formally passed pcv-1 artifacts.

Architecture, code quality and security framing: this is a big, cross-stack change involving authentication, persistence and irreversible external creation. The narrow template capability, sole credential owner, immutable operation identity, separate ACK fact and shared observation projector faithfully preserve the approved design. Channel remains a text-send abstraction. No accidental dual-write bridge, provider dispatch in domain services, background reconciliation or recipient-send expansion is evident. Large services and repeated UI fence checks increase maintenance difficulty; the finding identifies a concrete consequence rather than requesting cosmetic decomposition. Credential containment is operator-confirmed revocation or disablement, with known artifacts scrubbed and future CLI configuration isolation recorded. That does not establish historical absence of credential use or retract rendered output. SEC-R6-04 remains deferred through BLG-leadshug-template-recovery-read-budget and its recorded private-local-cohort restriction; unchanged sequential recovery load is not reopened here.

Test-quality cross-check: the owning surfaces are NestJS/Prisma/PostgreSQL and React/Vitest/Playwright. The project command is bash scripts/test-channels-local.sh all, which includes migration deploy/status, API lint/build/unit/PostgreSQL integration, Web build/unit and browser execution. The supplied terminal reports 284 API unit, 397 PostgreSQL, 31 Web unit and 58 Playwright cases. One Playwright case is explicitly pure consumer evidence. Browser tests use real session, CSRF, BFF, Prisma and PostgreSQL, with the provider network replaced externally; this does not establish live Meta compatibility. Production template composition remains exercised through the real resolver and adapter. Transaction fault injection delegates to actual PostgreSQL transactions; post-commit return errors are correctly distinguished from real database network failures. No silent live/mock fallback, ambient proof-subject selection, focused test, committed skip or test-only product endpoint is evident in the supplied changed tests. Browser response-loss injections follow real backend execution and are limited failure simulations, not provider-success evidence. The static status-only and spy signals require surrounding semantic assessment; the substantive tests also assert ownership, revisions, receipts, reservations, call counts and eligibility.

Fail-first classification: original feature coverage is test-after/unknown, consistent with accepted TQA-ST05-03 debt. The retained r7 eligibility failure is behavioral RED for its specific regression. Lint, compiler, fixture and host failures are not behavioral RED. No retrospective test-first claim is justified. Assertion efficiency is generally acceptable: large fixtures challenge bounded hydration, while the ten-second waits exercise the approved debounce. The new stale saved-observation write remains an uncovered response-order seam.

Command/platform/freshness matrix: disposable PostgreSQL and Linux/Node 22 Chromium browser validation are passed according to the supplied receipts. Source manifests and served-versus-dist hashes support attribution within this package; I did not execute commands or independently recompute them. Remote CI execution, preserved-database deployment, activated API/Web provenance and actual Meta submission/status remain pending. Other browsers, production capacity, delivery continuity and future networks are outside the claim. The activation plan preserves these gates and provides bounded metadata preflight, transactional migration timeouts and fail-closed handling without automatic repair.

Decision adherence: D01–D07 and D09 are substantially supported by the supplied implementation and evidence at candidate scope. D08 has the residual exception below. CR-01/CR-02 preserve observational GETs, explicit recovery, typed refusal and uncertainty without POST replay. AR-V11-01 has bounded indexed readback evidence; AR-V11-02 preserves global technical coordination and scoped business data; AR-V11-03 is supported by the recorded admission/seal attestations. CR-V11-01 has shared-fence producer and consumer evidence. No approved compatibility exception or non-goal requires reversal.

Five explicit test-method answers: (1) Changed assertions track real contract corrections, including unavailable eligibility, account-change copy and ACK provenance. (2) No demonstrated pass-the-test weakening appears; the debounce and required-fingerprint corrections are legitimate request preparation. (3) Assertions generally catch business regressions, with the finding's late state-write gap remaining. (4) Coverage is proportionate to the concurrency risks, with bounded fixtures and no capacity inference. (5) Candidate behavior has substantial layered coverage, while actual activation/provider proof and final delivery review remain required. This critique does not substitute for the separate complete TQA or security gate.
recommended_path: Accept the performance correction without another performance-driven redesign round. Route the nonblocking UI finding to the executor and adherence lane for a narrow fence correction and targeted regression. Preserve the private-cohort debt restriction and all pending activation, provider-proof, formal PCV and final-delivery gates.

findings.title: Late operation recovery can restore an observation into a different editor context
findings.rationale: In web-app/src/telas/Modelos.tsx, enviar's catch block executes the line restoreSavedObservation(recovered.savedObservation) immediately after awaiting templateApi.operation, before checking the captured contextEpoch and editorEpoch. A submission returning an operationId can start this read; switching BU, channel or draft while it is pending does not prevent its saved observation from updating the newly selected editor. The helper also compares fences across different remote IDs, although those fences belong to their captured contexts. A late observation can therefore display the previous account/model's status and eligibility in the current editor. This is fresh evidence in the revised saved-observation hydration path, distinct from the resolved form-replacement defect. It violates D08's response ownership requirement, but does not establish the severe server/runtime risk required for a blocking finding in this dispatch.
findings.suggested_action: A: move observation restoration behind the existing context/editor checks and validate the target draft/operation before applying it; recommended as the smallest correction. B: make the restoration helper require captured context/editor ownership so every asynchronous caller enforces the same rule. C: retain the code with an explicit D08 residual; not recommended because the correction is narrow. Verify with a real-BFF operation read carrying a nonnull savedObservation, hold its response, switch editor/context, then release it and assert that status, catalog membership and eligibility remain owned by the current selection; include A→B→A ordering.
